teaser: How our agent teams answer every row of a map of 190 agent identity projects: names, keys, behaviour policies and a signed record.
core_idea: Agent identity can be plain keys and files: a name that says who it acts for, a key per session, a behaviour policy for limits, and a signed record as reputation.

nodes.label: Maya Dotan's identity map
nodes.summary: 190 projects from 81 organisations, sorted by identity layer.

nodes.label: Dotted agent names
nodes.summary: role.speciality@team.person says what, which team and for whom.

nodes.label: A key per agent session
nodes.summary: P-256 keys, public halves in a registry, superseded with the time.

nodes.label: Who it acts for
nodes.summary: The person in the name and in every commit; only the person instructs.

nodes.label: Agent Behaviour Policy
nodes.summary: A grant of paths, tools and hosts and a never list, kept by hooks.

nodes.label: Approval at altitude
nodes.summary: Decisions as pages, drafts for irreversible acts, only the person merges.

nodes.label: Reputation as a record
nodes.summary: Signed run reports and reviews make trust a matter of evidence.

nodes.label: Enforcement is the hard part
nodes.summary: A limit kept only by the agent is a rule, not a control.

quotes.text: A good name answers three of her questions before any cryptography: which agent, which team, for whom.
Once every action is signed and recorded, reputation is the record
A limit kept only by the agent is a rule, not a control; the policy should say which is which.
